Stitch today

Stitch already sits inside millions of payments.

Stitch runs payments for thousands of South African merchants through one API: pay by bank, card, wallets, Pay Later, PayShap Request, payouts, refunds and in-person terminals. More than 6 million South Africans pay with Stitch.1 On 18 June 2026 Stitch launched the Stitch account for consumers: every payment in one view, rewards, Pay Later and a credit score.2 Mobile and data are not part of it yet.

6m+South Africans pay with Stitch1
1000sof merchants1
June 2026the Stitch account launched2
99.995%uptime1
What is at stake

A payment is a moment. The phone is every day.

Shoppers meet Stitch at checkout, then leave. The Stitch account needs a reason to be opened in the days between. Meanwhile every customer pays a network for their phone each month, and the network keeps the daily habit and pays out the rewards. Stitch Mobile brings that monthly payment, that daily habit and data as a reward into the Stitch account.

The idea

One Stitch SIM that works for every part of the business.

A network sells data. Only Stitch can turn every payment into it. Every feature of Stitch Mobile sends the customer back to something Stitch does.

The Stitch account

Free to use on every plan, with a Stitch Mobile tab for data, rewards and payments. Measured by weekly active accounts.

Pay by bank

The phone is paid by bank from the Stitch account. Measured by phone payments a month.

Rewards

Every Stitch payment earns GB on the customer's line. Measured by payments per line.

Pay Later

Out of data before payday, the customer takes data on Pay Later. Measured by Pay Later plans per line.

Fraud tools

The SIM is the customer's ID, RICA-verified, with SIM Signals alerts before money moves. Measured by fraud losses.

A new income line

Stitch keeps 50% of the net profit. Measured monthly, in rand.

The plans

Three plans, stitched into what Stitch already does.

Every plan answers one question: which part of Stitch does it grow? Weave and Quilt carry Bitdefender and a Personal Cyber Warranty from eInsurer, so customers' bank details are protected from scams. Stitch sets the final names and prices. Daily and weekly bundles can be shaped in the CVP workshop.

Plan prices are set by DSG MVNE for South Africa and include VAT at 15%. Bitdefender and the Personal Cyber Warranty are included at DSG's published prices and shared 50/50 with those partners. The mix of customers across plans is a DSG planning assumption for Stitch to replace with its own data.

What a customer gets

Customers get more for less, and things no network can give them.

MTN's 2.5GB data bundle costs R155, data only.3 Stitch Thread costs R149 and gives 3GB, 100 minutes, 50 SMS and the Stitch account free on top. Stitch Weave includes R64.47 a month of phone protection (Bitdefender R52.47 and a R10,000 Personal Cyber Warranty at R12). Stitch Quilt includes R139.64 (Bitdefender Family for 5 devices R115.64 and a R25,000 warranty at R24).

Signature ideas

Three ideas only Stitch plus a network can run.

Plans and prices are table stakes. These are the ideas customers would talk about. Each one drives a core Stitch line, and each is a proposal for Stitch to shape.

Pay, earn GBData becomes the Stitch reward

Every payment made with Stitch, while signed in to the Stitch account, earns GB on the customer's line. Paying by bank earns a bonus, four weeks running earns a streak, and merchants in the directory can fund double-GB days. Drives payment volume and account sign-ins. Needs a link to Stitch account payment events. Earn rates set by Stitch; base rewards funded from the network margin, boosts by merchants.

Never out at checkoutPaying with Stitch never needs data

The Stitch checkout and account are free to use on the Stitch SIM, so a shopper on Stitch Mobile is never cut off mid-payment. Out of data, they top up 1GB in one tap, by bank or on Pay Later. Drives completed checkouts for Stitch merchants, Pay Later plans and data sales by bank. Free use to be confirmed with the MVNE technical team; Pay Later follows Stitch's credit rules and a National Credit Act check.

SIM SignalsThe SIM is the customer's ID

Because Stitch runs the network, a SIM swap or a port on a Stitch Mobile line can pause a payout or a pay by bank approval until the customer confirms. Every line is RICA-verified. Drives lower fraud losses. The alert feed is to be confirmed with the MVNE technical team, used under POPIA with consent.

Proof

DStv Internet runs its network on our platform.

DStv Internet carries 9% of MTN's data traffic on the MVNE platform. DSG's own network, Digital Mobile, runs on the same platform, and MVNE has worked in the sector since 2013. Stitch Mobile would run on the same platform, with the same team.4

The numbers

Worth R51.2m to Stitch over five years, in the middle scenario.

Stitch does not publish how many people hold a Stitch account, so we ran three planning cases: 25,000, 50,000 and 100,000 lines by year 5. Even the largest is under 2% of the 6m+ South Africans who pay with Stitch. Move the slider to test any other size. Stitch's own numbers replace these in the CVP workshop.

Stitch's share by year

Year 1Year 2Year 3Year 4Year 5

DSG MVNE model, 60 months, rand, before VAT. Lines ramp to 10%, 30%, 55%, 80% and 100% of the year-5 target, starting with 2,000 customers at launch. Revenue assumes 88% of plan value is realised. Running costs include care, SIMs and RICA, Xanite offers and the MVNE fee of R7.50 a line or R75,000 a month. Net profit is shared 50/50. The R250,000 build fee is paid upfront by Stitch. Pay, earn GB rewards beyond the base allowance, merchant boosts and data on Pay Later are not in the model.
